passage.title: Khalid ibn al-Walid: Sword of Allah
paras: Khalid ibn al-Walid was born in Makkah into the Makhzum clan of the Quraysh. He was trained from childhood in horsemanship and the skills of battle, and he became one of the most gifted commanders of his time.

Before he accepted Islam, Khalid fought against the Muslims. At the Battle of Uhud in 625 CE, he led the cavalry charge that turned the battle. Later, he came to believe in the message of Islam and travelled to Madinah to accept Islam in about 629 CE.

In the same year, at the Battle of Mu'tah, the Muslim army faced a far larger force. Three commanders appointed by the Prophet ﷺ were killed one after another. Khalid took command, held the army together and brought it home safely. The Prophet ﷺ gave him the title Sayf Allah, a sword of Allah.

Under the caliphs Abu Bakr and Umar, Khalid led armies in Iraq and Syria, including at the Battle of Yarmuk in 636 CE. When Umar removed him from overall command, Khalid accepted the decision and continued to serve under another commander, showing that he fought for Allah rather than for his own position.
Khalid died in Homs, in Syria, in about 642 CE. He is remembered for his skill, his courage, and his obedience when it would have been easy to put himself first.
